> [!info] [[Eleanor David]]'s multimedia art project. Alex is advising on grant strategy and concept articulation. This note distills the concept; conversation-by-conversation history lives in the [[Eleanor David]] People note.
## Concept
A multi-character, multi-platform art project where each "character" is a different perspective/archetype. The viewer wanders a non-linear scavenger hunt across platforms; Eleanor is the museum tour guide.
**Core model (7 × 7 × 7):**
- **Seven archetypes** — Lila, Lacy, Elaine, and four others.
- **Seven mediums** — *the medium is the archetype.* e.g. Lila = short-form video (TikTok), Lacy = long-form (YouTube), Elaine = lecture series.
- **Seven galleries** — each platform is one gallery.
Platforms are intentionally **not cross-linked** — discovery happens through symbols and curiosity, not algorithmic threading. This is a hard creative constraint.
**The pivot:** Years of archetype-based *analysis* → "Museum of Seeing is the point at which I stopped explaining and started creating." (Earlier framed as "Museum of Small.")
## The keystone artifact
The **"map of the whole gallery"** — a premium / Easter-egg artifact available across all seven platforms. A single paid product common to every archetype, surfaced during the 5/13 workshop as the connective tissue the project was missing. By 5/18 this became a literal hand-drawn floor-plan and a physical board.
## Funding strategy
- **Primary target**: Charlotte Street Foundation (KC) **Virtual Producer Program** grant, $5–8K. Application largely complete — creative CV done, Canva portfolio (publishable as a website). Walked the Charlotte Street location in person to introduce herself.
- **Residency**: Jersey residency application due Tue 5/19 (folding new artifacts in).
- **Ideal scenario**: a single private patron — the medieval-Patreon model. Conceptual frame: **Musaion** (the Library of Alexandria's Shrine of the Muses) as the patron-protected gallery.
- **Open tension**: how to access funding ecosystems that demand quantitative metrics (followers, traffic, completed projects) for a project that is fundamentally about qualitative, internal sensation. She will not perform metrics.
## How she measures success (qualitative signals)
Past audience sent her their *own* original work in response: a published-author-adjacent piece, an Australian master's thesis on eroticism, a 12-minute YouTube response video, an AI-generated music album with her as the muse. These are her success signals.
## Stretch goals
Household name; three residences with full wardrobes (mountains / city / "southern peach"); redesigned social-media UX so one account can hold multiple voices.
## Alex's open coaching threads
- Three warm intros (nonprofit arts / grant writers / Kaufman-adjacent).
- Venue / studio / restaurant list she could record from.
- Suggest **AI deep research** (Claude/ChatGPT) for grant + residency hunting — no-cost win.
- Suggest she **reach back to her old audience-of-fans** — warm network already moved by her work.
- Watch the grant-proposal framing: it must *own the pivot* in one explicit sentence, or it reads as mid-pivot / indecisive.
## Timeline
- **5/4** — First strategy session (Roasterie Brookside). Concept walkthrough + three assignments to Alex.
- **5/13** — Grant-proposal workshop (~75 min). "Map of the whole gallery" breakthrough; 7 action items.
- **5/18** — Coworking check-in. Floor-plan map became a physical board; 3 of the action items executed.
- **5/19** — Jersey residency application due.
- **5/21** — Mystery-contact meeting (a Thursday contact she thought could help).
